blocks.md: FILTER = conditional aggregate without CASE. One scan, multiple aggregates with different conditions. Cleaner than SUM(CASE...), optimizer-friendly, index-friendly.

blocks.label: filter clause
blocks.code:
-- Count active employees per dept
SELECT dept_id,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'active') AS active_cnt,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'pending') AS pending_cnt,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'inactive') AS inactive_cnt
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept_id;

-- Equivalent CASE (verbose, less readable)
SELECT dept_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'active' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_cnt,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'pending' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pending_cnt
FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id;

-- Multiple aggregates, different filters
SELECT dept_id,
  AVG(salary) FILTER (WHERE status = 'active') AS avg_active,
  AVG(salary) FILTER (WHERE status = 'pending') AS avg_pending
FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id;
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL: no FILTER clause
-- Use SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)

before.performance: Single scan, optimizer can use indexes

options: All aggregate functions (SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, etc.)
items.explain: FILTER works with any aggregate: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, STRING_AGG, percentile, etc.

items.q: FILTER vs WHERE before GROUP BY:
options: FILTER keeps row for other aggregates; WHERE removes row entirely
items.explain: WHERE removes row from all aggregates. FILTER only affects that specific aggregate — row still contributes to others.

blocks.label: percentile functions
blocks.code:
-- Continuous percentile (interpolated)
SELECT percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) FROM employees;
-- Median

-- Discrete percentile (actual value)
SELECT percentile_disc(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) FROM employees;

-- Multiple percentiles
SELECT 
  percentile_cont(0.25) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS p25,
  percentile_cont(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS p50,
  percentile_cont(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS p75
FROM employees;

-- With GROUP BY
SELECT dept_id,
  percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS median_sal
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept_id;
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL 8.0+: PERCENTILE_CONT, PERCENTILE_DISC
SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) FROM employees;

blocks.md: percentile_cont = interpolated (may return non-existent value). percentile_disc = actual value from dataset. For median of even count: cont = avg of middle two, disc = lower middle.

items.explain: HyperLogLog probabilistic counter — O(1) memory, ~1-2% error.
Even count (4): cont interpolates between 20 and 30 = 25. disc = 20 (lower middle).

blocks.label: string_agg / json_agg
blocks.py-pandas:
# String aggregation
df.groupby('dept_id')['name'].apply(', '.join)

# With sort
df.sort_values('salary', ascending=False).groupby('dept_id')['name'].apply(', '.join)

# JSON
df.groupby('dept_id').apply(lambda x: x[['name','salary']].to_dict('records')).reset_index()

blocks.label: mode / stats
blocks.code:
-- Mode (most frequent value) — PostgreSQL 15+
SELECT mode() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY status) FROM employees;
-- Per group
SELECT dept_id, mode() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY status)
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept_id;

-- Standard deviation, variance
SELECT dept_id,
  STDDEV(salary) AS stddev,
  VARIANCE(salary) AS var
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept_id;

-- Correlation
SELECT CORR(salary, years_exp) FROM employees;
blocks.pg: -- mode(), stddev, variance, corr, covar_pop, regr_*

blocks.py-pandas:
# Mode
df.groupby('dept_id')['status'].agg(lambda x: x.mode().iloc[0] if not x.mode().empty else None)

# Stats
df.groupby('dept_id')['salary'].agg(['std', 'var'])

Discrete percentile — returns actual value from dataset at percentile.
